title: Inductive vs Electromeric Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A magnet holds a chain of paper clips: the first tight, the last barely. Diya's vinegar holds acetic acid, a weak acid, yet swapping one hydrogen for chlorine makes it almost eighty times stronger. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we see the pull that makes this happen.

On the molecule bench, chlorine pulls the shared pair along a carbon chain: delta minus, delta plus, double delta plus, triple delta plus, fading to almost nothing after three bonds. We sort -I and +I groups, watch a negative charge spread out to explain why chloroacetic acid is stronger, then see the pi pair of ethene and of a C=O shift fully when a reagent comes near (+E and -E) and snap back when it leaves. A worked example ranks chloroacetic, formic and acetic acid, then an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 84 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 A pull that fades
0:35 Delta charges and the inductive effect
1:07 The pull along a chain on the molecule bench
1:51 Why chlorine makes an acid stronger
2:36 Electromeric effect: +E and -E
3:26 Pause and think
3:46 Worked example: rank three acids
4:23 Exam trap
4:50 Practice question (JEE Main / NEET pattern)
5:24 Recap and three questions
